answer: To resist sybils, bind each identity to a unique quill: a hardware-attested enclave that must generate a fresh, non-reusable proof of unique computation before joining. An oasis of established validators verifies the proof and co-signs only if the computation fingerprint is novel. The velvet cost is the exclusive hardware slot and energy per proof; a farm cannot amortize one enclave across many keys because each quill burns its nonce and requires distinct physical silicon. Attackers pay linear hardware and energy per fake identity, while honest agents reuse their single device.
